the formation of two-dimensional cocrystals of 4, 4'-bipyryld and 1, 4-diiodotetrfluorobenzne was observed using synchrotrons X-ray diffraction, and that this is the first time that the I···N bond distance was measured in a two-dimensional crystal.

we have used synchrotron radiation to study the formation of a halogen-bonding monolayer on a graphite surface and that this has led to the first observation of a halogen bond in the monolayers of a halogen-containing molecule.

the formation of a 2D halogen-bonding network of 4, 4'-bipy and 1, 4-diiodotetrabenzene was observed at sub-monolayers using X-ray diffraction.
halogen-bonding is a viable and attractive alternative to conventional hydrogen-bonding for the formation of two-dimensional cocrystals on graphite surfaces.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the halogen bonding is a strong and directional intermolecular interaction that is capable of forming two-dimensional supramolecular structures at sub-monolayers on a solid surface.
we have observed, for the first-time, halogen bonding in the two-dimensional monolayer phase of a cocrystal.
we have observed, for the first, a two-dimensional halobonded cocrystals using the synchrotron diffraction technique.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the X-ray diffraction technique enables, for the first one, the measurement of the I···N distances in a 2D halogen-bonding cocrystal and identification of the halobonding interaction in the monolyer.
the halogen bonding interactions between 4,4′-bipyridyl (BIPY) and 1, 4-diiodotetrfluorobenzine (DTFB) molecules in a two dimensional layer are strong enough to form a monolayer cocrystal.
